experience.title: Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE)
experience.summary: Work directly with VA stakeholders on a healthcare claims platform with two frontends sharing a database, supporting claim submission, provider updates, claim progress and status tracking, and payment visibility.
highlights: Work with health providers to integrate APIs with the VA system so live claim statuses display for VA staff, providers, and veterans based on their role; the VA side previously had no continuously updated claim status.

Responded to stakeholder questions about stalled claims and process gaps by creating a claims framework that notifies the right party when a claim needs extra work, keeping claims moving and giving better tracking of every claim.

Built and continue to enhance Data Generator & File Processing because production data can't be used in VA lower environments. The team used to spend hours each day preparing data and keeping a database in every environment; now anyone can generate a full development database or up to 10,000 custom records in under 5 minutes, and the whole team uses it daily.

Run the tool like a product: versioned Windows releases built through GitHub Actions, in-app release notes, a user guide, a stakeholder overview, and release updates for the team; added Excel file processing with duplicate detection as a second workflow when team needs grew.

Enabled the team to use Tableau for requests and system information so any user can build their own dashboard; built custom dashboards for VA and internal users and, through repeated VA stakeholder discussions, expanded Tableau into the main way to monitor server health and system status.
Contribute React, TypeScript, and JavaScript features that turn stakeholder feedback into improvements to the claims application.

Work directly with VA stakeholders to map healthcare claims workflows, clarify technical and operational constraints, and define requirements and acceptance criteria for claim submission, provider updates, status tracking, and payment visibility.

Lead the stakeholder demonstrations at the end of each release cycle and program increment (since 2022) and all discussions with VA stakeholders; gather feedback on daily workflows and refine implementations around user needs.
Join working sessions with health-provider claims processors and, at times, VA end users on issues reported in production, to see the full picture and keep future work pointed in the right direction.

Investigate defects and data discrepancies across frontend, backend, and MySQL data; coordinate with developers and stakeholders to resolve delivery dependencies, and document progress, blockers, and operational impact in Jira.

Evaluated alternatives to legacy automation and helped select Playwright, weighing maintainability, reuse, authentication, and restricted environment access; developed a reusable smoke and regression framework that helps QA and developers reduce production bugs and deliver stakeholder requests faster.
Use GitHub Copilot in VS Code for development, debugging, refactoring, and test creation; use Gemini, GPT models, and Claude to explore implementation approaches.

projects.name: VA Claims Workflows
projects.description: Integrated health-provider claim-status APIs, built a claims-tracking framework and Tableau monitoring, and shipped React features on a VA healthcare claims platform, working directly with stakeholders and claims processors.
projects.challenge: VA stakeholders needed claim submission, provider updates, and payment visibility to work reliably across two frontends sharing a database. The VA side had no continuously updated claim status, claims could stall without anyone knowing why, and there was no single view of system and server health.
approach: Work directly with VA stakeholders to clarify claims workflows, requirements, acceptance criteria, and operational constraints.
Join working sessions with health-provider claims processors and, at times, VA end users on issues reported in production, to see the full picture and set the direction of future work.
Work with health providers to integrate APIs with the VA system so claim statuses display live for VA staff, providers, and veterans based on their role.

In response to stakeholder questions about stuck claims and process improvements, create a claims framework that notifies the right party when a claim needs extra work, so claims keep moving and can be tracked.

Enable the team to use Tableau for requests and system information; build custom dashboards for VA and internal users and expand Tableau's role, through repeated discussions with VA stakeholders, into the main source for monitoring server health and status.
Contribute React, JavaScript, and TypeScript frontend features supporting claim submission, provider updates, and status visibility.
Use MySQL to investigate discrepancies between application behavior and stored data across frontend and backend workflows.
Develop a reusable Playwright smoke and regression framework to validate claims workflows, reduce production bugs, and speed delivery of stakeholder requests.
Lead demonstrations at the end of each release cycle and program increment since 2022, incorporate stakeholder feedback, and coordinate defect investigations with developers.
projects.outcome: User-reported: live claim status now displays in the VA system for staff, providers, and veterans by role, where it was not continuously updated before; a claims framework notifies the right party so claims keep moving and are easier to track; and Tableau dashboards give VA internal staff a full view of system and server health. The Playwright framework helps QA and developers reduce production bugs and deliver stakeholder requests faster. These are not independently measured benchmarks.

Claims framework that keeps claims moving
Tableau dashboards for system and server health

projects.name: Data Generator & File Processing
projects.description: A Windows desktop app I built that generates realistic synthetic healthcare referral data on demand, then validates, packages, and uploads it, so developers and QA never need production records.
projects.challenge: Production data can't be used in test environments, so the team spent hours each day preparing data by hand and keeping a database in every environment. Developers and QA needed realistic referral records they could create on demand and tailor to each test.
projects.audience: Developers and QA teams who need realistic healthcare referral data to build and test workflows without production records.
approach: Built a generator that creates referral batches from one template, with unique referral numbers and patient IDs, current or custom dates, and facility, care package, and payment codes kept within valid reference lists.
Added processing for existing referral files: rewrite identities, dates, and reference values without touching the source files.
Automated batch handling: rename outputs, combine them into one master JSON, gzip the batch, and export a manifest with SHA-256 checksums.
Check the schema before processing and validate outputs against the selected reference values.
Upload results over SFTP to saved environment profiles, one target at a time, with remote size checks, per-target status, and retries for failed targets.
Added a second workflow when the team's needs grew: duplicate detection for the public HHS-OIG exclusion list (LEIE) Excel export, with example validation SQL.
Ship it like a product: versioned Windows installers built by GitHub Actions, in-app release notes, a user guide, and syntax, smoke, regression, and end-to-end UI tests.
projects.outcome: User-reported: the whole team uses Data Generator & File Processing daily. Work that took hours each day, plus keeping a database in every environment, now takes under 5 minutes for a full development database or up to 10,000 custom records, and developers rely on the same generated data in place of production records.
highlights: Full development database in under 5 minutes, used daily by the team
Up to 10,000 custom referral records per run
Validation, checksums, and SFTP delivery built in
Versioned installers, user guide, and automated tests
systems: Electron provides the desktop window, dialogs, and IPC between the interface and the Node.js processing logic.
One neutral referral template and JSON reference catalogs (facilities, care packages, payment authority codes) drive generation and validation.
Batch output is combined, gzipped, and described by a checksum manifest; SFTP upload profiles hold no credentials, which are imported at runtime and stored per user with OS encryption.
A GitHub Actions workflow builds the Windows installer; syntax, smoke, and regression checks run on any OS, and an end-to-end test drives the real Electron UI.
decisions: Every generated value is clearly synthetic (SSNs start with 999, phone numbers use 555-0xx, emails use example.com), so output can't be mistaken for a real person.
A desktop app keeps file selection, processing, and packaging local; the cost is Windows installation and update handling, solved with versioned installers and in-app release notes.
The upload queue tries each target once per run, keeps going after a failure, and offers explicit retries; completion checks the remote file size rather than trusting the transfer.
projects.relevance: This is how I handle a recurring team need: find where people lose time, build a tool for it, connect it to the systems it touches, and keep supporting it as the team relies on it.

evidence.label: Browse the source
evidence.detail: The public repository's README and docs cover the generator, file processing, validation, checksum manifest, SFTP upload, LEIE workflow, installer build, and test suite. All data in it is synthetic.

evidence.label: Reported team use
evidence.detail: Daily team adoption, the under-5-minute generation time, and the previous hours of daily preparation are user-reported outcomes, not independently measured public benchmarks.

projects.name: Claims Document Assistant
projects.description: An AI assistant that reads claim PDFs with Claude, pulls out 17 fields, flags missing or invalid information with fixed rules, and drafts the status reply for a person to review and approve.
projects.challenge: Claims examiners read every submitted document by hand to find the fields they need, check what is missing or wrong, and write back to the billing office. Documents arrive as forms, cover letters, and shorthand notes, so template-based extraction breaks as soon as the layout changes.
projects.audience: Claims-processing teams that review submitted documents and reply to billing offices, and the engineers who would evaluate an assistant like this before using it on real data.
approach: Send each claim PDF to Claude as a document block, with structured outputs constraining the answer to a fixed 17-field claim schema and an instruction to return null rather than guess.
Validate the extracted fields with deterministic rules, not the model: required fields, NPI check digits, ICD-10 and CPT formats, date order, expired referrals, and non-positive amounts.
Draft a short status reply from the rule findings, with a template fallback when no API key is set or the model call fails.

Queue every result for a person: the reviewer sees the PDF beside the fields, edits fields or the draft, then approves, escalates, or rejects. Corrections are re-validated and every decision is logged.
Route declined requests to manual review instead of returning an empty result.
Generate 60 labelled synthetic claim PDFs in three layouts, using the referral fields from Data Generator & File Processing, and score extractors against that ground truth.
projects.outcome: The assistant extracts, checks, and drafts replies end to end on synthetic data, and nothing goes out until a reviewer approves it. A 26-test suite covers the validation rules, the exact request sent to Claude, refusal handling, reply drafts, and the review queue. Claude's extraction accuracy has not been measured yet; the repository includes the evaluation command that will produce it.
highlights: 17 claim fields extracted from PDFs with Claude
Deterministic rules decide what is missing or invalid
Status reply drafted for review, never sent automatically
Review queue with audit log of every correction
60 synthetic claims in three layouts with ground truth
26 automated tests that run without an API key
systems: A generator produces seeded synthetic claim PDFs and their ground truth; every page is stamped as a synthetic test document.
The Claude extractor sends the PDF as a document block with a JSON schema. An offline rules extractor serves as a baseline and as a fallback without an API key.
A validation module applies the business rules; a drafting module writes the reply from the findings.
A local review server shows the queue, records each decision with the reviewer's name and changed fields in an append-only audit log, and writes only approved replies to an outbox.
decisions: The model extracts and drafts, but rules decide whether a claim is complete, so the outcome is predictable and testable.
A person approves every reply; the assistant never sends anything itself.

Synthetic data only. Using real claims would also need a provider agreement covering protected health information, access control on the review queue, retention rules, and an evaluation on a labelled sample of real documents.
Accuracy is reported only from the evaluation against ground truth. The rules baseline is published; Claude's results will be added once the evaluation runs with an API key.
projects.relevance: This is the kind of AI build I would bring to a healthcare or government team: the model handles messy documents, rules and a person stay in control, and every claim about accuracy comes from a measured evaluation.

evidence.label: Browse the source
evidence.detail: The public repository has the extractor, validation rules, review queue, synthetic data generator, evaluation script, and test suite, with a screenshot of the review queue in the README.

evidence.label: Measured results
evidence.detail: The README publishes the offline rules baseline. Claude extraction accuracy is not yet measured, so no AI accuracy figure is claimed here.

projects.name: Portfolio & Career Content System
projects.description: A React and Vite site where one validated career record drives this website, the browser resume, and the generated PDF and Word resumes.
projects.challenge: I needed my career facts to match across the website, a one-page resume, and a detailed resume without copying the same text into each one.
approach: Designed a schema-validated career record consumed by every presentation channel.
Rebuilt the portfolio on the official Untitled UI React and Vite stack, preserving static pages, content validation, and resume downloads.
Generated separate PDF and DOCX formats from the same factual source while preserving channel-appropriate layout.
Added strict diagnostics, static production builds, subpath packaging checks, and explicit deployment configuration.
projects.outcome: One publishing workflow keeps the site and every resume format in sync.
highlights: Designed one structured content architecture for every career presentation channel.
Redesigned the website with free Untitled UI React components while preserving static content and accessible navigation.
Added strict diagnostics, static production builds, subpath packaging checks, and explicit deployment configuration.
Prepared separate PDF and DOCX presentation contracts without duplicating career facts.
projects.audience: Recruiters and engineers looking at my work, and me, maintaining the resume formats.
systems: One career.json record supplies React pages, project routes, and resume content. A dependency-free schema check validates required fields before publishing.
React and free Untitled UI components render through Vite at build time. Browser hydration adds interactivity; core content and links are in the generated HTML.
Python produces PDF and Word resumes. Vite packages static assets for Cloudflare; a separate build verifies the /portfolio/ GitHub Pages base path. There is no runtime API or database.
decisions: Static rendering keeps content available before JavaScript runs and avoids a service/database to operate. Career changes require a rebuild.
One factual record reduces content drift. Web and print use separate layouts because native documents cannot run React components.
Cloudflare and GitHub Pages need different asset bases. Both builds are checked; configuration alone does not prove a production deployment.
projects.relevance: A public example of how I handle data contracts, UI, document generation, and deployment. My API and integration work is described in the work projects.
